rules: Class of title records the Registrar's confidence in ownership at registration.
Each registered estate or interest has a unique title number.
Every registered title has a title number, estate interest and class of title.
A pending registration can have a title number without estate-interest or class-of-title values.
The specification defines three classes of title for freehold land.
The specification defines four classes of title for leasehold land.
Absolute title is described as the best class of title.
A qualified title may be granted where a specific defect in title exists.
Possessory title may arise from adverse possession or lost or destroyed title deeds.
Good leasehold may be granted where evidence of the landlord's right to grant the lease is absent.
The tenure of a title does not change.
A non-absolute class can be upgraded when an application supplies the required evidence.
HMLR publishes a monthly full extract, change-only update and validation file for Title Descriptor data.
Title Descriptor files are available from the second working day of each month.

The Planning Data API exposes over 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
Latitude and longitude queries return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Multiple dataset parameters can be supplied in a single entity request.
For registered properties, querying by UPRN is described as more precise than a coordinate query.
No returned entity must not be treated as proof that no constraint exists because coverage varies.
Entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
The guide describes retrieving 337 local planning authorities in one request using limit 500.
The geometry_entity filter can restrict entities to those within another entity's geometry.
Listed-building entities include the grade field without a separate query.
Planning applications can be filtered with start-date components and start_date_match=since.
Custom WKT geometry coordinates must use WGS84, EPSG:4326.

Each contour tile includes a GML data file named from the tile reference.
Each contour tile includes an XML metadata file providing flying-date information.
Spot heights are selected automatically from the highest mass point within each closed contour.
A selected spot height is removed when its height equals the enclosing contour.
A spot height may be below the surrounding contour where a genuine depression exists.
Spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.

The source bare-earth surface excludes buildings, supported structures and vegetation.
